- When sentiment is negative (especially > -1.0) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >1.5% from prior day), model often overshoots downward in next 3–5 days — reduce forecast by 1–2% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., >0.5) after a downtrend, model often fails to fully recover — increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% of recent mean.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon — add 0.3–0.8% to forecast for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is flat (0.0) for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to drift toward mean — apply mean reversion bias toward 30-day moving average.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.5+), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
